tier: Standard (service_tier default) on the global endpoint https://api.openai.com/v1
rules: Input tokens include cached reads and cache writes: ordinary input = input - cached - cache writes (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching, checked 2026-09-25).
Cached input is 0.1x and cache writes 1.25x the uncached input rate. A model without a cacheWrite price bills cache writes as ordinary input.
longContext: prompts with more than 272K (read as 272,000) input tokens are priced at 2x input and cache rates and 1.5x output for the full request (each GPT-6 model page, checked 2026-09-25).

tiers: the gateway asks for service_tier default. A response served at another tier is multiplied: Flex 0.5x, Fast mode 2x (priority was renamed fast on 2026-07-30; responses report priority). A tier not listed here is charged at the highest listed factor.
Regional processing (data residency) endpoints add 10% and are not used. Batch is not used.
notes: There is no model named gpt-6: the GPT-6 family is gpt-6-astra, gpt-6-sol and gpt-6-luna (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/all, checked 2026-09-25).
There is no GPT-6 codex model. The newest codex model, gpt-5.3-codex, is listed for Responses-wire harnesses; OpenAI serves it on the Responses API only.
GPT-6 Sol and Luna call functions over Chat Completions only with reasoning_effort none (their model pages).

gpt-5-nano, round 2's cheaper second model, has no cache-write or long-context rates and no Fast mode price; its model page lists a 400,000-token context window with at most 272,000 input tokens (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5-nano, checked 2026-09-25).
confirmed: every price below was read on 2026-09-25 from both the pricing page and the model's own page, and they agree.
